chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q5 — Short Answer (4 points)
chunks.content: AP Chemistry Q5 (Short Answer), 4 points, one per part. Topic: analogous C and Si compounds (X vs Y) and gas laws. A [Pt1]: electron geometry around the central atom is tetrahedral. B [Pt2]: agree — compound Y (Si) has a larger, more polarizable electron cloud (more occupied electron shells) than X (C), giving stronger London dispersion forces and a higher boiling point. C [Pt3]: compound X has the higher vapor pressure at 82°C (weaker IMFs / X has reached its boiling point while Y has not). D [Pt4]: PV=nRT to find moles (≈0.744 mol). Common failure: attributing Y's stronger LDFs to molar mass instead of polarizability/electron-cloud size; stating agreement without a justification; adding molar masses instead of applying PV=nRT.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q5 exemplar — Sample 5A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q5 scored 4/4. Tetrahedral geometry (A); 'yes,' with Si having more electron shells and a more polarizable electron cloud than C (B); compound X higher vapor pressure with a valid boiling-point comparison at 82°C (C); moles via PV=nRT with supporting setup (D). Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q5 exemplar — Sample 5B, 3/4
chunks.content: Q5 scored 3/4. Earned A (tetrahedral), C (X higher vapor pressure, weaker IMFs), and D (correct moles; a minor R-value typo did not affect the three-sig-fig answer). Lost B: attributed Y's larger London dispersion forces to 'larger molar mass' rather than the larger, more polarizable electron cloud. Shows the frequent polarizability-vs-molar-mass justification error.

chunks.subject: AP Chemistry
chunks.title: Q5 exemplar — Sample 5C, 1/4
chunks.content: Q5 scored 1/4. Earned only C (X has the greater vapor pressure because it has reached its boiling point while Y has not). Lost A (did not identify tetrahedral geometry), B (agreed but gave no justification), and D (added molar masses instead of using PV=nRT). Illustrates a response holding only the vapor-pressure comparison.
